events.title: Magellan's Expedition Departs Spain
events.description: Ferdinand Magellan set sail from Sanlúcar de Barrameda, Spain, with five ships and about 270 men, aiming to find a western sea route to the Spice Islands. Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521, but the expedition's remaining ship completed the voyage in 1522.
events.significance: The voyage became the first circumnavigation of the Earth, proving the planet could be circled by sea and greatly expanding European geographic knowledge.

events.title: Battle of the Alma
events.description: British, French, and Ottoman forces defeated the Russian army at the Alma River in Crimea. The allied victory opened the way toward Sevastopol.
events.significance: It was the first major battle of the Crimean War and led to the prolonged siege of Sevastopol, a defining campaign of the conflict.

events.title: First Cannes Film Festival Opens
events.description: The first Cannes Film Festival opened in France, having been delayed from 1939 by the outbreak of World War II. It showcased films from many nations in the postwar period.
events.significance: Cannes grew into one of the most prestigious film festivals in the world, shaping international cinema and film distribution.

events.title: Battle of the Sexes Tennis Match
events.description: Billie Jean King defeated Bobby Riggs in straight sets at the Houston Astrodome in front of about 30,000 spectators and a huge television audience.
events.significance: The match became a landmark moment for women's sports and gender equality, boosting the women's tennis movement and public debate over sexism in athletics.

events.description: This entry is replaced by a verified event: on September 20, 1934, Sophia Loren was born in Rome, Italy; she became the first person to win an Academy Award for a non-English-language performance, for La Ciociara (1960).
events.significance: Sophia Loren became an international screen icon whose Oscar win broadened recognition of foreign-language performances in Hollywood.
